paragraphs.source_en: Then an old man, a keeper of an inn, said, Speak to us of **Eating and Drinking**.

units.source_en: Then an old man, a keeper of an inn, said, Speak to us of **Eating and Drinking**.

paragraphs.source_en: Would that you could live on the fragrance of the earth, and like an air plant be sustained by the light.

units.source_en: Would that you could live on the fragrance of the earth, and like an air plant be sustained by the light.

ja.t: われることができればよいのに。

paragraphs.source_en: But since you must kill to eat, and rob the newly born of its mother’s milk to quench your thirst, let it then be an act of worship,

paragraphs.source_en: And let your board stand an altar on which the pure and the innocent of forest and plain are sacrificed for that which is purer and still more innocent in man.

units.source_en: And let your board stand an altar on which the pure and the innocent of forest and plain are sacrificed for that which is purer and still more innocent in man.

paragraphs.source_en: “By the same power that slays you, I too am slain; and I too shall be consumed. For the law that delivered you into my hand shall deliver me into a mightier hand.

For the law that delivered you into my hand shall deliver me into a mightier hand.

paragraphs.source_en: And your fragrance shall be my breath, And together we shall rejoice through all the seasons.”

paragraphs.source_en: And in winter, when you draw the wine, let there be in your heart a song for each cup;

paragraphs.source_en: And let there be in the song a remembrance for the autumn days, and for the vineyard, and for the winepress.

paragraphs.source_en: For to be idle is to become a stranger unto the seasons, and to step out of life’s procession, that marches in majesty and proud submission towards the infinite.

units.source_en: For to be idle is to become a stranger unto the seasons, and to step out of life’s procession, that marches in majesty and proud submission towards the infinite.

paragraphs.source_en: When you work you are a flute through whose heart the whispering of the hours turns to music.

units.source_en: When you work you are a flute through whose heart the whispering of the hours turns to music.

paragraphs.source_en: Which of you would be a reed, dumb and silent, when all else sings together in unison?

paragraphs.source_en: But I say to you that when you work you fulfil a part of earth’s furthest dream, assigned to you when that dream was born,

paragraphs.source_en: But if you in your pain call birth an affliction and the support of the flesh a curse written upon your brow, then I answer that naught but the sweat of your brow shall wash away that which is written.
